pr_title: meson: make nologin path build time configurable
pr_body:
Some distros install nologin as /usr/sbin/nologin, others as
/sbin/nologin.
Since we can't rely on merged-usr everywhere (where the path wouldn't
matter), make the path build time configurable via -Dnologin-path=.

Closes #13028

"systemd-sysusers creates user systemd-coredump with shell /sbin/nologin, should be /usr/sbin/nologin"

In Debian and derived distros, `nologin` is installed as `/usr/sbin/nologin`. systemd hard-codes nologin at various places:

man/sysusers.d.xml:      a shell different <filename>/sbin/nologin</filename> must be used.</para>

Most of them are `/sbin/nologin`, some are `/usr/sbin/nologin`.

Since Debian and derived distros use `/usr/sbin/nologin` and Fedora/Redhat has merged-usr (i.e. doesn't care) I would propose to change the code to use `/usr/sbin/nologin` everywhere.
I'd be happy to provide a patch for that but wanted to check first (especially with other distros).
If other distros install `nologin` as `/sbin/nologin` and don't have `merged-usr`, I can either patch Debian downstream to use `/usr/sbin/nologin` or we make the path configurable.
So this is a RFC before working on a PR.
comments: Additional note: the path should be in /etc/shells. In Fedora both /sbin/nologin and /usr/sbin/nologin are. So yeah, I think we should do this, unless people from other distros raise objections. @fbuihuu?

urks, what a mess....

i guess on usr merged systems this doesn't matter... but debian is still a hold-out?
Right, just another pointless difference across distros. I'm just trying to make the best of it.
Gentoo has /sbin/nologin and does not have merged /usr.
I guess this means this needs to be build-time configurable as meson param. But yuck, I wished the holdouts would just stop being holdouts on this one.
@keszybz thanks for asking and no this shouldn't make any differences for openSUSE as both paths are available for them (/sbin/nologin is a symlink pointing to /usr/sbin/nologin).

BTW shouldn't we use the "downstream" label for this issue or is it supposed to be used for a different purpose ?

Another question: can one be subscribed automatically for issues with a given label set ?

Thanks

> BTW shouldn't we use the "downstream" label for this issue or is it supposed to be used for a different purpose ?

I'm not sure what `downstream` is supposed to mean, really. `downstream/fedora` or `downstream/debian` is clear. Maybe we should just kill `downstream` label?

> Another question: can one be subscribed automatically for issues with a given label set ?

Nope. This could probably be scripted, and would be really useful for cases like this.
Maybe we could keep it and use it for issues/discussions like this one which affect all distros ?
But almost all bugs affects all distros... There are some "upstream" bugs, e.g. relating to process or CI or such, but they are the minority. That's why I think the "downstream" label is useless.
Thanks for the feedback. I'll work on a PR then which makes this build-time configurable.

review_comments: hmm, this is needlessly cryptic. Maybe NOLOGIN_PATH would be a better name, matching the existing MOUNT_PATH and UMOUNT_PATH?

We are not consistent here. While we have `MOUNT_PATH` and `UMOUNT_PATH`, we also have `TELINIT`, `SULOGIN`,  `KMOD`, etc without a _PATH suffix. The latter seems more commonly used , which is why I picked the shorter version without the path. I can change it to `NOLOGIN_PATH` though if you prefer.
That's because there's already MOUNT macro (for casting units). I think NOLOGIN is appropriate. (Or we should change all of them to have the `_PATH` suffix.)

So the thing that trips me up is that there's also /etc/nologin + /run/nologin, and it's awfully confusing to have all this and then be so short that we just have NOLOGIN?

Maybe call this NOLOGIN_BINARY to make clear it's not about those other files we also manage?
Which specific part of the code becomes hard to read? Not quite sure which place you mean with /etc/nologin + /run/nologin, tbh.

do git grep "nologin" in our sources and you'll see nologin_timeout_handler() and related code in logind and tmpfiles that handles a /run/nologin file that has almost nothing to do with the nologin binary... It's UNIX fault I guess, but I think we should probably work towards keeping them as separete as we can, and in particular for global defines avoid just referring to anything as just "NOLOGIN", since it's not obvious what that is: it could be the path to /run/nologin or the path to /usr/sbin/nologin, the name doesn't help you at all, and we refer to both paths in our codebase. Hence, let's avoid the confusion, and work towards cleaning this up at least a bit, by naming this #defined NOLOGIN_BINARY or so, which make this very clear to grok

(i mean, let's not forget that /run/nologin also moved from one path to another, so it's very similar territory, so the uninitiated reader might very well assume that the NOLOGIN macro refers to that variable path, even though it refers to a very different concept and variable path)
If we are not going to use an existing naming scheme for this variable, maybe `NOLOGIN_SHELL` would be best to indicate what it is about?
